# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel (dual-run) for the duration of the migration. Users are migrated in batches by phase; the legacy system remains fully operational as a fallback until all migration phases are complete and validated. Decommissioning of the legacy system is explicitly out of scope for this plan and must not occur until a separate, subsequent decommissioning phase begins after the final migration batch is confirmed stable.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — ~800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full parity testing in staging (invoice generation, tax calculation, payment retries, and refunds match legacy output for a synthetic dataset of ≥5,000 transactions with 0 discrepancies), and dual-write/dual-read reconciliation tooling is live in production.

**Composition:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (no active disputes, no complex multi-subscription accounts, standard payment methods only).

**Duration:** 1–2 weeks, with daily reconciliation checks.

---

## Phase 2: Expanded Early Adopters (15% of users — ~6,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed with billing error rate ≤0.1% and zero critical (P1) incidents for 5 consecutive days; support ticket volume attributable to migration is within 1.5x of baseline.

**Composition:** Random stratified sample across customer segments (geography, plan tier, payment method) to surface edge cases before broad rollout.

**Duration:** 2–3 weeks.

---

## Phase 3: General Rollout (50% of users — ~20,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed with billing error rate ≤0.1%, payment failure rate not elevated more than 0.5 percentage points versus legacy baseline, and all P1/P2 defects from Phase 2 resolved or have verified workarounds.

**Composition:** Remaining standard accounts migrated in waves of ~5,000, sequenced by lowest-risk segments first (e.g., monthly billing before annual/enterprise contracts nearing renewal).

**Duration:** 3–4 weeks, with wave-over-wave go/no-go checkpoints.

---

## Phase 4: Final Batch and Long-Tail Closure (33% of users — ~13,200 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 completed with billing error rate ≤0.1% sustained across all waves, finance has reconciled Phase 3 revenue against legacy figures within 0.05% variance, and legacy system remains fully operational and untouched (no deletion, disabling, or decommissioning actions occur in this phase — that is reserved for a separate post-migration decommissioning phase after this batch is validated).

**Composition:** Remaining users, including complex enterprise accounts, active-dispute accounts, and edge-case billing configurations requiring manual review.

**Duration:** 4–6 weeks, followed by a minimum 30-day stabilization/observation window before any legacy system decommissioning planning begins.

---

## Halt Metric

If the billing error rate (defined as invoices with incorrect amount, duplicate charge, or failed reconciliation entry, divided by total invoices processed) exceeds **0.5% in any rolling 24-hour window** for users on the new system, the rollout is halted immediately: no further users are migrated until root cause is identified and a fix is verified in staging. Additionally, halt if customer-reported billing disputes increase by more than **3x baseline daily average** in any 24-hour period.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missed charges during dual-run reconciliation due to timing mismatches between old and new system billing cycles | Implement idempotency keys and a reconciliation job that flags any transaction not matched in both systems within 1 hour, with automated alerting | Billing Platform Engineering Lead
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are migrated incorrectly, causing invoice disputes and revenue leakage | Require manual finance sign-off and side-by-side invoice comparison for every enterprise account before migration in Phase 4 | Finance Operations Manager
RISK: Payment method tokens fail to migrate correctly, causing failed renewals and involuntary churn | Run a token validation dry-run against the payment processor sandbox for 100% of accounts in each phase before cutover, and monitor payment failure rate against baseline | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by migration-related tickets, delaying detection of systemic issues | Stand up a dedicated migration support queue with escalation SLAs and pre-written macros for common issues, staffed ahead of each phase | Customer Support Director
RISK: Rollback from new system to old system mid-phase causes data loss or double billing for affected users | Define and test a rollback runbook per phase in staging, including data reconciliation steps, before that phase begins | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

PHASES: 4
